label: verify-bm-mycelium-living-materials

claims.claim: The only measured in-air humidity data for a mycelium layer of bilayer relevance is Nie 2026: T. versicolor film, two grown layers, E = 23.7 MPa, volumetric expansion 9.27% (A) vs 3.38% (B) between 30% and 85% RH, 0.22-0.30 mm per layer (contains PVA and glycerol).
claims.source_says: Bulk moisture expansion rate (ε_b) was higher for layer A (9.27%) than layer B (3.38%); 30% RH dry scan to ~85% RH; 10% PVA + 10% glycerol, E 23.7 MPa; thickness 0.22 and 0.30 mm.
claims.note: All numbers and the PVA/glycerol content check out, but 'the only measured' is a universal claim the source cannot support (the source itself cites Sinha et al. on living S. commune films).

claims.claim: A micrometre-thin layer of dried microbial cells is the largest humidity-strain living layer with a fitted model: volume linear in RH, 1 um cells on 200 um latex bends at 15% RH and flattens at 95% RH, fitted modulus 70 MPa.
claims.source_says: The top layer is composed of E. coli cells (1 μm thick), and the bottom layer is a latex sheet (200 μm thick). It bends at 15% RH and becomes flat at 95% RH. Fitted elastic modulus of the cell layer is 70 MPa.
claims.note: Geometry, linear volume-RH and 70 MPa are in the source, but the source does not rank this as the largest humidity strain among living layers.

claims.claim: Particulate mycelium composites are a poor swelling layer: water uptake 6-436%, drying shrinkage 2.78-17%, swelling almost all through-thickness (205-244%), in-plane under about 7%, poor wet integrity.
claims.source_says: in-plane dimensional changes were limited, with width and length changes generally remaining below approximately 7%. Review: 436% in rapeseed straw; Ganoderma on beech sawdust (6%); MBC shrinkages between 2.78% and 17%.
claims.note: Each number is in its cited text (205-244% are formulation 2 means at 2 h and 72 h, and formulations 1 and 7 lost integrity); 'poor swelling layer' is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Shen 2024 reaches 160 MPa modulus and 0.72 MPa tensile strength only on a coarse paste-printed substrate (2 mm layers) and the living phase weakens that substrate; no growth on a Formlabs resin published.
claims.source_says: our method yields the strongest mycelium composite reported to date with a modulus of 160 MPa and tensile strength of 0.72 MPa
claims.note: 160/0.72 MPa confirmed in the Europe PMC abstract; the 2 mm layer, weakening and Formlabs absence are not in the abstract or the arXiv abstract page (arXiv text not opened by me), and the absence claim is a negative.

overall: The numbers in the four key claims reproduce against their sources (Nie, Wang, hemp-hurd and review texts, Shen abstract). Each of the three that go beyond numbers adds an overreach the sources do not carry: 'only measured', 'largest', and the Shen 2 mm layer/weakening/no-Formlabs details, which I did not confirm in the full text.
